category: Graphs III: Construction, Styling, Random Graphs & Trees
description: Named and parametric graph families, random-graph distributions, graph annotation options (labels, styles, weights, capacities, coordinates, layouts), vertex/edge indexing and adjacency lists, the Tree expression type introduced in 12.3 with its construction, traversal and editing functions, and relation/expression graphs.

tools.name: GraphLayout
tools.description: Option of Graph, GraphPlot and related functions choosing the vertex layout algorithm: "SpringElectricalEmbedding" (default), "SpringEmbedding", "CircularEmbedding", "LayeredDigraphEmbedding", "LayeredEmbedding", "RadialEmbedding", "SpectralEmbedding", "PlanarEmbedding", "TutteEmbedding", "BipartiteEmbedding", "MultipartiteEmbedding", "StarEmbedding", "GridEmbedding", "LinearEmbedding", "BalloonEmbedding", "DiscreteSpiralEmbedding", "SphericalEmbedding", "HighDimensionalEmbedding" and more, with sub-options such as "RootVertex", "Orientation" and "Dimension". GraphEmbedding returns the coordinates a layout produces.
tools.usage:
Graph[edges, GraphLayout -> "CircularEmbedding"]
Graph[edges, GraphLayout -> {"LayeredDigraphEmbedding", "Orientation" -> Left}]
Graph[edges, GraphLayout -> {"RadialEmbedding", "RootVertex" -> 1}]
GraphEmbedding[g]
GraphEmbedding[g, "SpectralEmbedding", 3]

parameters.name: GraphLayout
parameters.description: Layout name or {name, suboptions}; also accepts "Dimension" -> 3 for 3D layouts.

tools.name: VertexLabels
tools.description: Graph annotation options: VertexLabels ("Name", "Index", a property name, or rules v -> Placed[label, pos]), EdgeLabels ("Name", "EdgeWeight", "EdgeTag", rules), VertexLabelStyle and EdgeLabelStyle for their formatting. Labels can be arbitrary expressions, including images and Tooltips.
tools.usage:
Graph[edges, VertexLabels -> "Name"]
Graph[edges, VertexLabels -> Placed["Name", Center], VertexSize -> 0.3]
Graph[edges, VertexLabels -> {1 -> "start", 5 -> Placed["end", Above]}]
Graph[edges, EdgeLabels -> "EdgeWeight", VertexLabelStyle -> Directive[Bold, 12]]

parameters.name: VertexLabels
parameters.description: None, "Name", "Index", Automatic, property name, or rules.

tools.example: Graph[{1 <-> 2, 2 <-> 3}, EdgeWeight -> {2.5, 1.0}, VertexLabels -> "Name", EdgeLabels -> "EdgeWeight"]

tools.name: VertexStyle
tools.description: Styling options: VertexStyle and EdgeStyle (colours/directives globally or per element via rules), VertexSize (absolute, Scaled or per-vertex), VertexShape / VertexShapeFunction (custom vertex graphics, e.g. images or named shapes "Square", "Hexagon"), EdgeShapeFunction (custom edge drawing, "CurvedArc", "Arrow" variants) and GraphStyle (named theme). Combine with HighlightGraph for emphasis.
tools.usage:
Graph[edges, VertexStyle -> Red, EdgeStyle -> Dashed]
Graph[edges, VertexStyle -> {1 -> Green, 2 -> Blue}, VertexSize -> {1 -> 0.4}]
Graph[edges, VertexShapeFunction -> "Square", EdgeShapeFunction -> "CurvedArc"]
Graph[edges, VertexShapeFunction -> (Inset[img, #1, Center, 0.5] &)]
Graph[edges, GraphStyle -> "DiagramGold"]

parameters.name: VertexShapeFunction
parameters.description: Named shape or function of (position, vertex, size).

parameters.name: EdgeShapeFunction
parameters.description: Named style or function of (coordinates, edge).

tools.example:
g = CycleGraph[6];
Graph[g, VertexSize -> Medium, VertexStyle -> Thread[VertexList[g] -> ColorData[97] /@ Range[6]], EdgeStyle -> Thick, GraphStyle -> "ThickEdge"]

tools.name: EdgeWeight
tools.description: Graph property options: EdgeWeight (numbers used by shortest-path, flow, spanning-tree and centrality functions), VertexWeight, EdgeCapacity and VertexCapacity (for flow problems), EdgeCost (for FindMinimumCostFlow) and VertexCoordinates (explicit positions). Values are given as a list in EdgeList/VertexList order or as rules; read them back with PropertyValue, AnnotationValue or WeightedAdjacencyMatrix.
tools.usage:
Graph[edges, EdgeWeight -> {w1, w2, ...}]
Graph[edges, EdgeWeight -> {e1 -> w1, ...}]
Graph[edges, VertexCoordinates -> {{x1, y1}, ...}]
Graph[edges, EdgeCapacity -> caps, VertexCapacity -> vcaps]
PropertyValue[{g, e}, EdgeWeight]
AnnotationValue[{g, e}, EdgeWeight]

parameters.name: EdgeWeight
parameters.description: List or rules of numeric weights.

tools.name: WeightedAdjacencyGraph
tools.description: Builds a weighted graph from a weight matrix (Infinity or a given value marking non-edges), the inverse of WeightedAdjacencyMatrix; use it to import distance matrices, cost tables and correlation networks as graphs.
tools.usage:
WeightedAdjacencyGraph[wmat]
WeightedAdjacencyGraph[{v1, v2, ...}, wmat]
WeightedAdjacencyGraph[wmat, DirectedEdges -> True]
WeightedAdjacencyMatrix[g]

parameters.name: wmat
parameters.description: Matrix of weights; Infinity (or the SparseArray background) means no edge.

tools.name: AdjacencyList
tools.description: AdjacencyList gives the neighbours of a vertex (or of all vertices, optionally within distance k) and IncidenceList the incident edges; VertexIndex and EdgeIndex map vertices/edges to their positions in VertexList/EdgeList, which is how results of centrality or coordinate functions are aligned with vertices. KirchhoffMatrix gives the graph Laplacian.
tools.usage:
AdjacencyList[g, v]
AdjacencyList[g, v, k]
AdjacencyList[g]
IncidenceList[g, v]
VertexIndex[g, v]
EdgeIndex[g, e]
KirchhoffMatrix[g]
tools.example:
g = GridGraph[{3, 3}];
AdjacencyList[g, 5] (* {2, 4, 6, 8} *)
cent = BetweennessCentrality[g]; cent[[VertexIndex[g, 5]]]
Eigenvalues[N[KirchhoffMatrix[g]]] (* Laplacian spectrum *)

tools.name: StarGraph
tools.description: Parametric graph families beyond CompleteGraph/GridGraph/CycleGraph/PathGraph/KaryTree: StarGraph, WheelGraph, TreeGraph (from a list of edges or as a random tree), CompleteKaryTree, HypercubeGraph, TorusGraph, CirculantGraph, ButterflyGraph, DeBruijnGraph, TuranGraph, HararyGraph, KnightTourGraph, CayleyGraph, PetersenGraph and BuckyballGraph. All accept the standard graph options.
tools.usage:
StarGraph[n]
WheelGraph[n]
TreeGraph[{e1, e2, ...}]
CompleteKaryTree[n, k]
HypercubeGraph[n]
TorusGraph[{m, n}]
CirculantGraph[n, {j1, j2, ...}]
DeBruijnGraph[m, n]
PetersenGraph[n, k]
CayleyGraph[group]
tools.example:
HypercubeGraph[4]
PetersenGraph[7, 2]
CayleyGraph[DihedralGroup[4]]
CirculantGraph[8, {1, 3}]

tools.name: RelationGraph
tools.description: Builds the graph of a binary relation f over a list of vertices (edge u -> v when f[u, v] is True), the quickest way to turn any predicate (divisibility, subset, similarity threshold, string distance) into a graph; ExpressionGraph shows the tree structure of an expression as a graph and NestGraph iterates a function to generate a graph.
tools.usage:
RelationGraph[f, {v1, v2, ...}]
RelationGraph[f, {v1, ...}, {w1, ...}]
ExpressionGraph[expr]
NestGraph[f, expr, n]
tools.example:
RelationGraph[EditDistance[#1, #2] == 1 &, {"cat", "cot", "cut", "cog", "dog"}, VertexLabels -> "Name"]
ExpressionGraph[a x^2 + Sin[b x]]
NestGraph[{2 #, 3 #} &, 1, 3]

tools.name: BernoulliGraphDistribution
tools.description: Random-graph models for RandomGraph and GraphPropertyDistribution: BernoulliGraphDistribution (G(n, p)), UniformGraphDistribution (G(n, m)), BarabasiAlbertGraphDistribution (preferential attachment), WattsStrogatzGraphDistribution (small world), PriceGraphDistribution (citation), SpatialGraphDistribution (geometric) and DegreeGraphDistribution (given degree sequence). Use them for null models and synthetic benchmarks.
tools.usage:
RandomGraph[BernoulliGraphDistribution[n, p]]
RandomGraph[BarabasiAlbertGraphDistribution[n, k]]
RandomGraph[WattsStrogatzGraphDistribution[n, p, k]]
RandomGraph[SpatialGraphDistribution[n, r]]
RandomGraph[DegreeGraphDistribution[{d1, d2, ...}]]
RandomGraph[dist, m]

parameters.name: p / k / r
parameters.description: Model parameters: edge probability, edges per new vertex / neighbours, connection radius.

tools.name: GraphPropertyDistribution
tools.description: Represents the distribution of a graph property (e.g. GraphDiameter[g], EdgeCount[g]) under a random-graph model, so that Mean, Variance, Probability, NProbability and RandomVariate can be applied - the standard way to compute expectations and p-values for network statistics against null models.
tools.usage:
GraphPropertyDistribution[prop, g \[Distributed] dist]
NExpectation[prop, g \[Distributed] dist]
NProbability[cond, g \[Distributed] dist]

parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: Expression in the graph symbol g.

tools.name: PropertyValue
tools.description: Reads or sets properties (weights, styles, labels, custom keys) of a graph or of individual vertices/edges: PropertyValue[{g, v}, prop], SetProperty[{g, v}, prop -> val] returns a modified graph, PropertyList lists the available properties; AnnotationValue / Annotate are the newer general forms that also work for meshes and other annotated objects. Use them to attach and query metadata.
tools.usage:
PropertyValue[{g, v}, VertexWeight]
PropertyValue[{g, e}, EdgeWeight]
SetProperty[{g, v}, VertexStyle -> Red]
SetProperty[g, {VertexLabels -> "Name"}]
PropertyList[{g, v}]
AnnotationValue[{g, e}, EdgeWeight]
Annotate[{g, v}, "Population" -> 10^6]

parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: Standard property symbol or custom string.

tools.name: TreePlot
tools.description: Draws a graph or list of rules as a tree (choosing a root automatically or as given), with orientation control; LayeredGraphPlot3D and GraphPlot3D give 3D layouts and TreeGraph builds tree graphs. For the Tree expression type use TreeForm/Tree display instead.
tools.usage:
TreePlot[g]
TreePlot[{a -> b, a -> c, ...}]
TreePlot[g, Top, root]
TreePlot[rules, Left, root, VertexLabels -> "Name"]

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Root placement: Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Center.

tools.example: TreePlot[{1 -> 2, 1 -> 3, 2 -> 4, 2 -> 5, 3 -> 6}, Top, 1, VertexLabels -> "Name"]

tools.name: Tree
tools.description: Tree[data, {subtree1, ...}] represents a rooted, ordered tree whose nodes carry arbitrary data (introduced in 12.3) - the native structure for hierarchies such as JSON, XML, file systems and parsed expressions. Trees display graphically, support TreeQ, and have a full toolkit for construction (RulesTree, ExpressionTree, NestTree, RandomTree, GraphTree, FileSystemTree), access (TreeData, TreeChildren, TreeLeaves, TreeExtract, TreePosition), transformation (TreeMap, TreeFold, TreeInsert, TreeDelete, TreeReplacePart) and measurement (TreeDepth, TreeSize).
tools.usage:
Tree[data, {t1, t2, ...}]
Tree[{t1, t2, ...}]
Tree[data, None] (* leaf *)
Tree[<|k1 -> t1, k2 -> t2|>]
TreeQ[expr]

parameters.name: {t1, ...}
parameters.description: Child trees (elements that are not Tree objects become leaves); None marks a leaf.

tools.example:
t = Tree["root", {Tree["a", {1, 2}], Tree["b", None], 3}]
TreeData[t] (* "root" *)
TreeLeaves[t] (* {1, 2, 3} *)
TreeDepth[t] (* 2 *)

tools.name: ExpressionTree
tools.description: Converts a Wolfram Language expression into a Tree (with "Heads", "Atoms", "Subexpressions" or "HeldHeads" node conventions), and RulesTree converts nested rules {root -> {child -> {...}, ...}} into a Tree; TreeExpression is the inverse conversion back to an expression. Use ExpressionTree to inspect or manipulate expression structure visually, replacing TreeForm for programmatic work.
tools.usage:
ExpressionTree[expr]
ExpressionTree[expr, "Heads"]
ExpressionTree[expr, "Subexpressions"]
RulesTree[root -> {child1 -> {...}, child2}]
TreeExpression[tree]
TreeExpression[tree, "Heads"]
tools.example:
t = ExpressionTree[a x^2 + b, "Heads"];
TreeLeaves[t] (* {a, x, 2, b} *)
TreeExpression[t, "Heads"] (* a x^2 + b *)
RulesTree["animals" -> {"mammals" -> {"cat", "dog"}, "birds" -> {"owl"}}]

tools.name: TreeData
tools.description: Accessors for Tree objects: TreeData (root data), TreeChildren (list of child subtrees), TreeLeaves (data of all leaves in depth-first order), TreeExtract (subtree or data at a position), TreePosition (positions matching a pattern), TreeDepth, TreeSize (number of nodes). Positions are lists of child indices like Part specifications.
tools.usage:
TreeData[tree]
TreeChildren[tree]
TreeLeaves[tree]
TreeExtract[tree, {i, j, ...}]
TreeExtract[tree, pos, f]
TreePosition[tree, patt]
TreeDepth[tree]
TreeSize[tree]

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Position as a list of child indices ({} is the root).

tools.example:
t = RulesTree[1 -> {2 -> {4, 5}, 3}];
TreeExtract[t, {1, 2}] (* subtree at child 1, grandchild 2: Tree[5, None] *)
TreePosition[t, _?EvenQ] (* {{1}, {1, 1}} *)
TreeSize[t] (* 5 *)

tools.name: TreeMap
tools.description: TreeMap applies a function to the data of every node (optionally only at given levels or positions, and with TreeTraversalOrder control), TreeFold folds a function over the tree bottom-up (the general tree reduction, e.g. evaluating an expression tree), and TreeScan applies for side effects. These are the functional core of Tree processing.
tools.usage:
TreeMap[f, tree]
TreeMap[f, tree, levelspec]
TreeMap[f, tree, All, TreeTraversalOrder -> "BreadthFirst"]
TreeFold[f, tree]
TreeFold[{f, g}, tree]
TreeScan[f, tree]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function applied to node data (TreeMap) or to {data, list of child results} (TreeFold).

tools.example:
t = RulesTree[Plus -> {1, Times -> {2, 3}}];
TreeFold[If[#2 === {}, #1, Apply[#1, #2]] &, t] (* 7 *)
TreeMap[ToString, t]
TreeMap[f, t, "Leaves"]

tools.name: TreeInsert
tools.description: Structural editing of Trees: TreeInsert adds a subtree at a position (with index among the children), TreeDelete removes subtrees at positions, TreeReplacePart replaces subtrees, and Tree options TreeElementLabel / TreeElementStyle / TreeLayout control how nodes are displayed. Use them to build and edit hierarchies programmatically.
tools.usage:
TreeInsert[tree, subtree, {pos, i}]
TreeDelete[tree, pos]
TreeDelete[tree, {pos1, pos2, ...}]
TreeReplacePart[tree, pos -> subtree]
Tree[..., TreeElementLabel -> {pos -> label}, TreeElementStyle -> {pos -> style}, TreeLayout -> "Radial"]

parameters.name: i
parameters.description: Child index at which to insert.

tools.example:
t = RulesTree[1 -> {2, 3}];
t2 = TreeInsert[t, Tree[4, None], {{}, 2}] (* insert as second child of root *)
TreeDelete[t2, {1}]
TreeReplacePart[t, {2} -> RulesTree[9 -> {8}]]

tools.name: NestTree
tools.description: Generates a Tree by repeatedly applying a function that maps node data to a list of children (n levels), the tree analogue of NestGraph; RandomTree generates random trees, GraphTree converts a tree-shaped Graph (from a root) into a Tree and FileSystemTree builds the directory tree of a path. Useful for game trees, search trees and file browsers.
tools.usage:
NestTree[f, data, n]
RandomTree[n]
RandomTree[n, k]
GraphTree[g]
GraphTree[g, root]
FileSystemTree[dir]
FileSystemTree[dir, depth]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function giving the list of children data of a node.

tools.example:
NestTree[{2 #, 2 # + 1} &, 1, 3] (* binary heap indices *)
FileSystemTree[$InstallationDirectory, 1]
GraphTree[CompleteKaryTree[3, 2], 1]

tools.name: TreeOutline
tools.description: Displays a Tree as an indented, collapsible outline (text form) instead of the graphical node-and-edge rendering - practical for large trees such as file systems or JSON structures; TreeForm remains the classic expression-tree graphic and TreeGraph converts a Tree to a Graph.
tools.usage:
TreeOutline[tree]
TreeOutline[tree, "Open"]
TreeGraph[tree]
tools.example:
TreeOutline[RulesTree["root" -> {"a" -> {1, 2}, "b" -> {3}}]]
TreeGraph[RandomTree[20]]

tools.name: TreeTraversalOrder
tools.description: Option of TreeMap, TreeScan, TreeFold, TreeLeaves, TreePosition and related functions selecting the traversal: "TopDown" / "BottomUp" (depth-first pre/post order, the defaults), "BreadthFirst", "DepthFirst", {"Order", spec} with "Reversed"/"Alternating" variants. Determines the order in which side effects occur and in which TreeLeaves lists data.
tools.usage:
TreeMap[f, tree, TreeTraversalOrder -> "BreadthFirst"]
TreeScan[Print, tree, TreeTraversalOrder -> "BottomUp"]
TreeLeaves[tree, TreeTraversalOrder -> "BreadthFirst"]

tools.name: IncidenceGraph
tools.description: Constructs a graph from an incidence matrix (vertices x edges, entries 1/-1 or 2 for loops), the inverse of IncidenceMatrix; together with AdjacencyGraph and WeightedAdjacencyGraph it covers construction from all standard matrix representations, e.g. when importing graphs from numerical libraries.
tools.usage:
IncidenceGraph[imat]
IncidenceGraph[{v1, v2, ...}, imat]
IncidenceGraph[imat, DirectedEdges -> True]
tools.example:
im = IncidenceMatrix[CycleGraph[4]];
IsomorphicGraphQ[IncidenceGraph[im], CycleGraph[4]] (* True *)

tools.name: MeshConnectivityGraph
tools.description: Builds the connectivity graph of a MeshRegion (vertices connected by mesh edges, or cells of a given dimension adjacent when they share a face), linking computational geometry to graph algorithms - e.g. shortest paths on a triangulated surface or FindGraphPartition for mesh decomposition. MorphologicalGraph does the analogue for skeleton images.
tools.usage:
MeshConnectivityGraph[mesh]
MeshConnectivityGraph[mesh, d]
MeshConnectivityGraph[mesh, {d1, d2}]
MorphologicalGraph[image]

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Cell dimension whose adjacency is used (default 0 = vertices).

tools.name: DirectedEdges
tools.description: Option of Graph, RandomGraph, AdjacencyGraph, RelationGraph and other constructors specifying whether edges given as rules or matrices are directed (True), undirected (False) or inferred (Automatic). Also the EdgeList/EdgeRules forms: EdgeRules[g] returns edges as rules u -> v for use with other functions.
tools.usage:
Graph[{1 -> 2, 2 -> 3}, DirectedEdges -> False]
RandomGraph[{10, 20}, DirectedEdges -> True]
AdjacencyGraph[m, DirectedEdges -> True]
EdgeRules[g]
tools.example:
g = AdjacencyGraph[{{0, 1, 0}, {0, 0, 1}, {1, 0, 0}}, DirectedEdges -> True];
EdgeRules[g] (* {1 -> 2, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 1} *)
